topIssues.body:

-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Cannon doesn't have perfect MIPS compatibility, it makes sense to deprioritize anything that we know isn't contained in the compiled `op-program`. But dependency updates might contain unexpected additions of unsupported functionality, and it would be good to have a warning.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A safety checker, enforcing something similar to Rust's `no_std` attribute. It could use Go [SSA](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/ssa). @protolambda has a [Go SSA callgraph analyzer](https://github.com/protolambda/gocyto), this would be similar but suitable for CI with error output listing unexpected calls.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I haven't considered alternative solutions yet.

**Additional context**

topIssues.title: Contract Versioning Tool
topIssues.author: tynes
topIssues.body:
<!--
Need help?
Refer to our contributing guidelines for additional information about making a good issue:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

We pretty consistently have issues with semantic versioning of the smart contracts. A tool that can be used to manage semver would be very helpful here, it should be expected to be able to list the semver of all of the contracts as well as automatically bump semver of contracts in different ways (patch, minor, major, beta).

There would be a few commands like `list`, `bump <contract name> <type>` where it would automatically modify the source code of the contract directly and `release` where it would accept a list of candidate contracts to release and automatically remove the `beta` tag.

There are a few ways to think about the `list` command. My thinking is that it should work on the foundry artifacts rather than the source code, since we publish artifacts as releases. This command has a few ways that it could operate. All solutions likely involve a first step where the ABIs are scanned through, looking for contracts that implement `IVersion`
- ~~Look through the source code directly of the contracts for the `IVersion` and use string parsing to pull out the version.~~ The source code is not included in the artifacts, perhaps the `build-info` but its difficult to work with that file
- Embed the deployed bytecode in a stateless EVM and perform a single call to get the version
- Look at the natspec docs in the compiler output
I think its best to not look at the natspec since a bug could result in 2 different values, plus this will not work for the feature contracts that extend the base contracts since the real semver lives in the base. Running a simple call makes the most sense.

For the `bump` command, we will want to operate on the source code itself. We could reuse infra for the `list` command to determine the version and then use string manipulation to update the file directly.

For the `release` command, we will want to provide a list of contracts and then use the same infra as the `bump` command but instead trim any `beta` tags.

The snapshots could be ran after this and then CI should pass easily.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: fast finality mode (prove without waiting for a challenge)
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Ports fast finality mode from op-succinct's fault-proof proposer (@ 13716c2c): with FAST_FINALITY_MODE=true the proposer proves every game it owns while the game is still unchallenged. A proven game is over immediately, so it resolves as soon as its parent does instead of waiting out maxChallengeDuration: proof spend traded for finality latency. Off by default.

Closes #22112, part of #21463. Stacked on #22121 (defend path); GitHub retargets when it merges.

## What is upstream and what is ours

Ported:
- Resume scan + creation capacity gate in should_create_game (upstream :2098-2203): count ALL in-flight proving tasks (defense included) against FAST_FINALITY_PROVING_LIMIT; below the limit, spawn proving for owned InProgress+Unchallenged games without one (restart recovery, pre-mode backlogs, and every newly created game one tick after creation); at the limit, skip creation this tick ("never create games faster than they can be proven").
- Deadline semantics: should_skip_proving now takes Option<deadline> and keys its warning window by task kind (maxProveDuration for defense, maxChallengeDuration for fast finality). A game past its challenge deadline is not proven: it resolves DefenderWins for free.
- Env knobs, defaults, startup-log fields: FAST_FINALITY_MODE (false), FAST_FINALITY_PROVING_LIMIT (1).

Adapted, with reasons:
- The fast-finality set is prestate-based; upstream's gameCreator == signer filter is dropped (option A, #22111: prove set = resolve set = claim set). Consequence, documented in the README: an unchallenged foreign game with a known prestate is proven at this proposer's expense (no bond upside), and proposers sharing prestates duplicate spend; run one fast-finality proposer per prestate set. Upside: post-rotation old-key games keep fast finality. Pinned by a unit test (creator-foreign, prestate-owned game IS proven).
- Candidates come from cached state: no per-candidate gameCreator RPC (upstream does a live read per game).
- The skip check stays at call sites (defend-path shape) instead of inside spawn; scan order is deadline-ascending for determinism; scan errors propagate (upstream warn-continues; impact is one skipped tick).
- New kona_sp1_proposer_games_fast_finality_spawned gauge (upstream has no FF-specific metric).
- FAST_FINALITY_PROVING_LIMIT is a NonZeroU64: zero is rejected at parse time, matching the defense-cap convention from the base branch (upstream would silently never create a game again; a zero limit would silently never create one either).
- pre_submit_checks (a defend-path divergence; upstream submits blind) now accepts Unchallenged as well as Challenged: the public values bind the signer, not the status, so a challenge landing mid-proof does not invalidate the proof (and the reverse reorg is equally fine). Still rejects proof-provided and Resolved.

Dropped, with evidence:
- Upstream's creation-time spawn (create_game :1424-1432). It is dead code in both codebases: the spawn fires before the game enters the state cache (only the sync loop inserts games), so upstream's own "Game not in cache" arm skips it; our prove_game abandons untracked games the same way. The scan is the actual proving mechanism in both; effective proving start is one FETCH_INTERVAL tick after creation (30s default, 2s in devstack), immaterial against multi-minute proving and a 30-60 minute challenge window. Porting it would ship a guaranteed no-op task per creation and double-count the spawn metric.
- spawn_game_proving_task's Ok(bool) return shape: call sites track spawned-vs-skipped directly.

## Concurrency interaction (also in the README)

| Situation | Effect |
|---|---|
| active proving tasks (defense + fast finality) >= limit | no new fast-finality proving; game creation paused this tick |
| defense tasks alone >= limit | same: defense load pauses creation (upstream parity) |
| fast-finality tasks in flight | never count against MAX_CONCURRENT_DEFENSE_TASKS |
| game challenged while a fast-finality proof is in flight | proof stays valid; per-game dedup prevents a second task (pinned by unit test) |
| a fast-finality proof keeps failing at the limit | creation stays paused until it succeeds or is classified unprovable; game_proving_error is the spend alarm |

## Test plan

- Rust: 96 unit tests (was 86), including the scan capacity/dedup/ownership pins, the capacity gate counting defense tasks, the creator-foreign inclusion pin, the awaiting_proof status table, and the duration-selection wiring; clippy --all-features --all-targets --locked, lint-docs, and typos clean.
- Go: gofmt and op-golangci-lint clean; sysgo TestZKProposerOptions pins the option-to-env mapping.
- Acceptance (sysgo, mock provider): full zk suite green, 10 existing tests plus new TestProposerFastFinalityProvesAtCreation: game 0 reaches UnchallengedAndValidProofProvided with NO challenge, the proposer is the prover, and the game resolves DefenderWins BEFORE its challenge deadline with no L1 time travel before resolution (every other test advances L1 past the deadline first).
- As with the defend path: no SPN calls and no SNARK cryptography in any test; the fast-finality path reuses the defend-path proving pipeline unchanged.

topPRs.title: op-devstack: prevent one stalled dial from consuming ConnectP2P's whole budget
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
_Requested via [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C03N11M0BBN/p1785473115249889)_

## Description

Root-cause fix for the `TestFollowSource_P2PSync` flake tracked in #22152 ([CI job 5404179](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/131541/workflows/a4da9120-7bf0-4112-b577-41a05efb828d/jobs/5404179), `develop` @ `8970404b`).

**What happened:** the devp2p peering succeeded ~5s into `ConnectP2P`'s 30s verification window, but the test failed with `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:40135: i/o timeout` — the sequencer op-reth's user-RPC `tcpproxy` listener. The go-ethereum websocket RPC client found its connection dead on the first `admin_peers` poll and re-dialed; geth's reconnect bounds the dial only by the call context, which `ConnectP2P` shares across the whole `wait.For` loop — and `wait.For` aborts on the first callback error. Result: one loopback TCP connect the kernel never answered (accept loop provably alive — its exit is logged inside the same millisecond as `Close()` at teardown) consumed the entire budget, with the harness structurally unable to retry from a fresh source port. Full analysis in #22152.

## Changes

**`op-service/testutils/tcpproxy/proxy.go`**
- `handleConn` no longer holds the proxy mutex across the upstream dial. Previously every newly accepted connection's data path — plus `SetUpstream` and `Close` — serialized behind any slow upstream dial, and `net.Dial` is not cancelled by the `retry.Do` context (only checked between attempts), so a single unanswered upstream SYN could hold the lock for ~2min of kernel SYN retries. Dials are now per-attempt context-bounded and lock-free; connection registration re-checks `stopped` under the lock, preserving the `Close()` guarantee.
- The upstream dial function is an injectable unexported field (defaults to the real dialer) so tests can hold a dial in flight deterministically, and in-flight dials are parented on a proxy lifecycle context that `Close` cancels, so `Close` never waits out a stalled dial.
- `SetUpstream` contract is connection-level: accepted/in-flight connections keep the upstream they captured; updates affect future accepts only. No generation/cancellation machinery.
- The accept loop closes (rather than leaks) a successfully accepted conn when exiting on stop.
- Added `proxy_test.go` (package previously had no tests): echo round-trip, 32-way concurrent connections, unreachable-upstream behavior + recovery after `SetUpstream`, prompt `Close` with in-flight connections, and two red/green tests that hold one upstream dial in flight and assert `SetUpstream`, a second connection's data path, and `Close` all progress before the held dial is released, plus the captured-upstream contract.

**`op-devstack/sysgo/l2_el_p2p_util.go`**
- `ConnectP2P`/`DisconnectP2P` verification polls now bound each `admin_peers` call individually (5s) and retry — within the unchanged 30s budget — only genuine attempt timeouts: the attempt deadline must have expired while the outer budget is live **and** the returned error must itself be a context/network timeout, since the RPC client can return an unrelated error while the attempt deadline happens to be expired. A fresh attempt dials from a fresh source port, which is exactly what the failing run needed. Any other error (connection refused, RPC error) still fails fast per the no-papering-over rule.
- The retained attempt-timeout error is attached to the final failure only when polling ends because the outer budget expired; a later permanent error is returned unchanged so `errors.Is`/`As` cannot misclassify it as a timeout.
- Added `l2_el_p2p_util_test.go`: behavioral tests for the poll helper via a fake `RpcCaller` (interval and attempt timeout are explicit parameters of the unexported `pollPeerList`).

## Red/green verification

All new regression tests were run mechanically against the old implementations (details preserved in the review-response comment):

- tcpproxy: old `proxy.go` from parent `8970404bb5` + only the dial seam, new tests unchanged → `TestProxyStalledDialDoesNotBlockProxy` and `TestProxySetUpstreamAffectsOnlyFutureConns` both FAIL (`SetUpstream blocked behind an in-flight upstream dial`). Green on the fixed implementation.
- sysgo: with `pollPeerList` reverted to the previous PR-head logic, `TestPollPeerListFailsFastOnRPCError` FAILS (error retried 100× instead of failing fast) and `TestPollPeerListPermanentErrorAfterTimeoutIsNotWrapped` FAILS (terminal error chain contains the stale `context deadline exceeded`). Green on the fixed logic. The remaining two tests cover the retry and outer-budget paths.

## Caveats

The precise kernel-level reason this one loopback SYN went unanswered for ~30s (≈5 retransmissions) could not be reproduced deterministically from a single occurrence — candidates (accept-backlog overflow vs. listener-side `TIME_WAIT` 4-tuple collision from the proxy's active closes) are discussed in #22152. What this PR fixes are the verified harness defects that turned a transient per-4-tuple connect blackhole into a hard 30s setup failure, without widening any budget.

## Tests

- `go test ./op-service/testutils/tcpproxy/... -race -count=3` — pass
- `go test ./op-devstack/sysgo/ -run 'TestPollPeerList' -race -count=3` — pass (run with a locally generated placeholder `superchain-configs.zip` to satisfy the pre-existing embed gap in this environment; nothing committed)
- `go vet` on both changed packages — pass; `gofmt` clean
- `go build ./op-service/...` — pass; full `go build ./...` is blocked in this environment only by the pre-existing `op-core/superchain/superchain-configs.zip` embed gap, unrelated to this diff

## Metadata

- Fixes #22152

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests: cover kona-sp1 proposal safety
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Extends ZK dispute game acceptance coverage for the kona-sp1 proposer’s game-creation path.

New scenarios verify that the proposer:

- adopts a valid foreign game,
- defers classification while the super-root RPC is behind, and
- rejects both invalid games and otherwise-valid descendants of invalid ancestry.

## Bugfix

This change also fixes a bug in the kona-sp1-proposer where it extends an invalid game (with a valid output root but invalid parent) because it forgot the invalid parent game. The proposer now remembers invalid subtrees until factory history resets.

## Devstack changes

ZK tests now use an explicit `WithZK()` preset with targeted overrides for proposal cadence. The preset also resolves one SP1 vkey for both game deployment and proposer artifacts, avoiding mismatched configuration.

Also adjusted the default zk challenge and prove durations to reduce flakiness

Related: #18326

topPRs.title: op-node: Wake the driver loop when sequencer actions are armed
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
`Sequencer.Start` and `Sequencer.Stop` run on the `admin_startSequencer`/`admin_stopSequencer` RPC goroutine and set `nextAction`/`nextActionOK` directly. The driver event loop only reads that schedule at the top of an iteration (`planSequencerAction`), and is otherwise parked in its `select`, so arming an action never woke it. A freshly promoted sequencer therefore idles past its first block deadline until an unrelated wakeup arrives — the L1 head poll, the unsafe-gap ticker (`2 * BlockTime`), or a derivation step — and then builds late. `Stop` had the mirror problem: the armed timer survived the stop and fired a stale sequencer action afterwards.

The sequencer now signals a capacity-1 channel while holding the lock that guards the schedule, and the event loop selects on it. Because the driver re-reads the whole schedule on every iteration, signals coalesce; the send is non-blocking, so the RPC goroutine is never held up. `planSequencerAction` also forgets the deadline when it disarms, so re-arming on the same instant still resets the timer instead of tripping the "avoid unnecessary timer resets" check.

### Evidence

Two op-conductor logs from one CircleCI job (pipeline 131344, job 5391956), L2 block time 1s:

- `sequencer2` logs `Sequencer has been started ... "next action"=15:43:10` at `15:43:10.836`, but the driver does not log `Scheduled sequencer action delta=-242.538596ms` until `15:43:11.079` — **243 ms late**, woken by an unrelated event. Being ~1 block-time behind, it then sealed block 13 at `11.082` and block 14 at `11.085`: two blocks in 3 ms.
- In the other run `sequencer2` is active from `15:43:55.641` to `15:43:56.528` — an **887 ms window spanning a block's due time with no sequencer action logged at all**. When `sequencer1` took over at `15:43:56.529` its first action came at `15:43:56.954`, `delta=-425.270491ms`.

Found while root-causing `TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC` (ethereum-optimism/optimism#22094). The op-conductor fix for that flake is a separate PR and does not depend on this one.

This removes the 0–2 s of avoidable lag after promotion, but it does not remove catch-up burst-building: the chain is still behind wall clock by the failover duration itself (1.657 s in the log above), and `onForkchoiceUpdate` deliberately starts the next block instantly while `payloadTime - now <= blockTime`. Whether that catch-up is desirable is a separate policy question, deliberately untouched here.

### Test plan

The new driver tests run a real `eventLoop` with every incidental wakeup source quiesced (block time set so the unsafe-gap ticker is 2 h), so the only thing that can wake it is the sequencer signal. On `develop` `TestEventLoopWakesWhenSequencerStarts` and `TestEventLoopSignalDuringPlanIsNotLost` hang until their 30 s deadline, and `TestEventLoopWakesWhenSequencerStops` fails at 250 ms with a stale sequencer action.

Also run: `go test ./op-node/rollup/driver/... ./op-node/rollup/sequencing/... -count=3 -race`, `go test ./op-e2e/actions/sequencer/... -count=1`, and `go test ./op-e2e/system/conductor/ -run TestSequencerFailover -count=3`. `TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC` still flakes at roughly its `develop` rate (2/10 with this change, 3/10 on `develop` locally) — that is ethereum-optimism/optimism#22094, addressed elsewhere.
